mainTopic: Worry when a family or group member dies; whether destructive acts (מקלקל), especially חובל and מבעיר, are exempt on שבת; the measure of a double סיט; and the start of the משנה on trapping.
overview: This amud opens by finishing a short אגדה: when one brother or one member of a group dies, everyone else should worry and examine their deeds. There are two versions of whether this applies more when the oldest dies or when the youngest dies. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's rule that anyone who does a מלאכה destructively (מקלקל) on שבת is exempt. רבי אבהו cites a ברייתא that makes wounding (חובל) and kindling (מבעיר) exceptions. רבי יוחנן rejects that ברייתא, or else limits it to cases where the act is useful, such as needing the blood for a dog or needing the ashes. The גמרא explains that the משנה follows רבי יהודה and the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון. רבי שמעון learns his view from the verse that permits מילה on שבת and from the ban on burning a בת כהן on שבת. רבי יהודה answers that both of those acts are constructive, as רב אשי explains. The גמרא then shows two ways to measure the double סיט for whitening. Finally, a new משנה about trapping a bird or a deer begins, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: When one dies, the whole family or group should worry
steps.stepSummary: If one brother dies, all the brothers should worry. If one member of a group dies, the whole group should worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the brothers should be worried. If one member of a group dies, the whole group should be worried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a short אגדה from the previous discussion. When one person in a family or group dies, the others should take it as a warning and look at their own deeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that one person's death may be a sign of judgment that is coming on the whole family or group. So the survivors should not feel safe. They should do תשובה.

keyTerms.meaning: They should worry or be concerned
Brothers
A group or fellowship of people

phrases.english: all of the brothers should be worried.
phrases.notes: This continues a case from the previous lines, where one of the brothers died.

phrases.english: One member of a group who dies —
the entire group should be worried.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues an אגדה that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The death of one member of a family or group is a warning to all the others.

steps.title: Dispute over whether the oldest or the youngest is meant
steps.stepSummary: Some say the worry applies when the oldest dies. Others say it applies when the youngest dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say this is when the oldest dies, and some say it is when the youngest dies.
steps.whatsHappening: Two opinions are recorded about which death should cause the most worry: the oldest's or the youngest's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the oldest, who has the most merit, died, then the others are surely not protected. If the youngest died, that may be the beginning of a punishment that will spread to everyone. Both views agree that the others should worry. They only disagree about which case is the strongest warning.

keyTerms.meaning: The oldest or greatest
The youngest or least

steps.whatToRemember: A death in a family or group is a call for everyone to do תשובה. The two versions only argue over whether the oldest's or the youngest's death is the clearer sign.

phrases.english: Some say it refers to when the oldest dies,
and some say it refers to when the youngest dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies which case Step 1 is mainly about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two versions: the worry is strongest when the oldest dies, or when the youngest dies.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: destructive acts are exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that anyone who does a מלאכה in a destructive way on שבת is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And all those who act destructively are exempt."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, a person is only liable for a מלאכה that builds or improves something (מלאכת מחשבת). A מקלקל only damages, so the משנה exempts him. The next steps ask whether there are exceptions to this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: People who act destructively, damaging rather than improving
Exempt from liability (no חטאת is brought)

steps.confusionAlert: פטור here means exempt from punishment or a קרבן. It does not mean the act is allowed on שבת.

phrases.english: And all those who act destructively are exempt.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה, introducing the topic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the אגדה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who does a מלאכה destructively on שבת is exempt.

steps.title: רבי אבהו's ברייתא: wounding and kindling are exceptions
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו recited a ברייתא before רבי יוחנן. It says all destructive acts are exempt except חובל and מבעיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו taught before רבי יוחנן: All those who act destructively are exempt, except for one who wounds and one who kindles a fire.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו brings a ברייתא that agrees with the משנה's general rule. However, it adds two exceptions: wounding and kindling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this ברייתא, someone who wounds a person or lights a fire on שבת is liable even if the act is purely destructive. This seems to contradict the משנה's rule that every מקלקל is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him, in his presence
One who wounds and causes bleeding
One who kindles a fire

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu taught before Rabbi Yochanan:
All those who act destructively are exempt
except for one who wounds and one who kindles.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that adds exceptions to the משנה's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Destructive wounding and destructive kindling are liable on שבת.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rejects the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells רבי אבהו to take this teaching outside, because the part about חובל and מבעיר is not an accepted teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go teach it outside. Wounding and kindling is not a valid teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן rejects the exceptions in רבי אבהו's ברייתא. He says they are not reliable enough to be taught in the בית מדרש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that the main rule, that all מקלקלין are exempt, has no exceptions. The clause listing חובל and מבעיר should be dropped.

keyTerms.meaning: Go teach it outside, meaning it is not accepted here
It is not an authoritative teaching

phrases.english: He said to him: Go out and teach it outside,
wounding and kindling is not a valid teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוחנן rejects the ברייתא from Step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the clause about the exceptions (חובל and מבעיר).
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It goes against the accepted rule that every מקלקל is exempt.

steps.title: If the ברייתא is accepted, it is about useful wounding and kindling
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא is valid after all, it refers to wounding when the person wants the blood for his dog, and kindling when he wants the ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want to say it is a valid teaching: the one who wounds needs the blood for his dog, and the one who kindles needs the ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן offers a second option. If we must keep the ברייתא, we read it as cases where the act is not really destructive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the person wants the blood or the ashes, the act accomplishes something useful, so he is no longer a מקלקל. This way the ברייתא does not argue with the משנה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want to say (introduces a fallback answer)
His dog
Its ashes

phrases.english: And if you want to say it is a valid teaching —
one who wounds is when he needs the blood for his dog,
one who kindles is when he needs its ashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a fallback reading instead of rejecting the ברייתא completely.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא makes destructive wounding and kindling liable.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about constructive cases, so it fits the משנה.

steps.title: How can the ברייתא contradict our משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי אבהו could recite such a ברייתא, since the משנה clearly says all מקלקלין are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in the משנה: All those who act destructively are exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבהו's ברייתא. It points out that the ברייתא directly conflicts with our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a blanket exemption with no exceptions. A ברייתא should not contradict it unless the two follow different תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in a משנה)? Introduces a challenge from a משנה

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
All those who act destructively are exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא from Step 4 using the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה exempts every מקלקל, but the ברייתא makes חובל and מבעיר liable. They contradict each other.

steps.title: The משנה and the ברייתא follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי יהודה, and the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה is רבי יהודה; the ברייתא is רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is no contradiction. The two sources simply reflect two different תנאים who disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה exempts every destructive act, with no exceptions. רבי שמעון holds that wounding and kindling are liable even when done destructively. The next steps explain why רבי שמעון holds this.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
A teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה

phrases.english: Our Mishnah follows Rabbi Yehuda,
the baraita follows Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, בָּרָיְיתָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the sources to different תנאים (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and the משנה contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: They follow different תנאים: the משנה is רבי יהודה and the ברייתא is רבי שמעון.

steps.title: What is רבי שמעון's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון makes destructive wounding and kindling liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי שמעון's source. This question sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a destructive act liable goes against the usual rule for מקלקל. So the גמרא wants to see where in the Torah רבי שמעון learns it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי שמעון's view from Step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source showing that destructive wounding and kindling are liable.

steps.title: Source for wounding: the verse permitting מילה on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The Torah needed a verse to permit מילה on שבת. This shows that wounding in general is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since a verse was needed to permit circumcision, it follows that wounding in general is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי שמעון's source for wounding. If wounding were never liable, the Torah would not need a special verse to allow מילה on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fact that the Torah had to permit מילה proves that, without that verse, the wound of מילה would be forbidden. So ordinary wounding on שבת is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: A verse was needed
Circumcision
In general, in ordinary cases

phrases.english: Since a verse was needed to permit circumcision,
this shows that one who wounds in general is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 9 for the case of wounding.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The special permission for מילה shows that wounding is otherwise liable.

steps.title: Source for kindling: the burning of a בת כהן
steps.stepSummary: The Torah forbade kindling for the execution of a בת כהן on שבת. This shows that kindling in general is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And since the Torah forbade kindling for a בת כהן, learn from it that kindling in general is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי שמעון's second source, this time for kindling. Even kindling a fire to carry out the death penalty of a בת כהן is forbidden on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The execution of a בת כהן is a destructive kind of burning, yet the Torah still forbids it on שבת. So kindling is liable even when it is destructive.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Kindling a fire
A כהן's daughter, executed by burning for adultery
Learn from it

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, חובל and מבעיר are exceptions to the rule that a מקלקל is exempt. He learns this from מילה and from the burning of a בת כהן. Our משנה follows רבי יהודה, who exempts every מקלקל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This סוגיא explains why some sources make destructive wounding and kindling liable while others do not.

phrases.english: And since the Torah forbade kindling
regarding the execution of a priest's daughter,
learn from it that one who kindles in general is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדַּאֲסַר רַחֲמָנָא הַבְעָרָה גַּבֵּי בַּת כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to Step 9 by giving the source for kindling.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון's view that destructive kindling is liable.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Torah's ban on kindling for the execution of a בת כהן on שבת.

steps.title: How does רבי יהודה answer these proofs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה handles רבי שמעון's proofs from מילה and the burning of a בת כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? (How does he deal with these proofs?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי יהודה and asks how he responds to the two proofs just brought for רבי שמעון. This short question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that every מקלקל is פטור. The verses about מילה and the burning of a בת כהן seemed to show that wounding and kindling are חייב even when destructive. So רבי יהודה needs a way around these proofs.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda? (How does he deal with this?)
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא's usual short way of asking how the other side answers this proof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the opposing view answers the proofs given in steps 10–11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי יהודה, who exempts all מקלקלין, explains the proofs from מילה and the burning of a בת כהן.

steps.title: Those cases are constructive acts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה answers that מילה and the execution by burning are not destructive at all. They are constructive (מתקן), as רב אשי explains.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is a constructive act, as רב אשי explained.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יהודה: the cases in those verses are really acts of fixing, not destroying. It points to רב אשי for the explanation, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון learned from these verses that destructive wounding and kindling are חייב. רבי יהודה says the proof does not work, because מילה and the burning are constructive. So the verses only teach about constructive acts, and nothing can be learned about מקלקל.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in those cases)
One who fixes or improves; a constructive act
In line with what רב אשי said

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהודה denies that wounding and kindling are מלאכות. He agrees they are. He only says these particular cases are constructive, so they cannot prove anything about destructive acts.

phrases.english: There, it is a constructive act,
as Rav Ashi explained.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the source cases are constructive, not destructive.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מילה and burning the condemned are destructive acts, so the Torah's need for verses shows that מקלקל is חייב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both acts are מתקן, so the verses teach nothing about מקלקל, and רבי יהודה can still hold that all מקלקלין are פטור.

steps.title: רב אשי: circumcision fixes, and melting the wick is like cooking dyes
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that מילה is like repairing a vessel, and heating the lead wick for the execution is like cooking dye herbs in the משכן. Both are constructive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: What difference is there to me between repairing through מילה and repairing a vessel? And what difference is there to me between cooking a wick and cooking herbs?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב אשי's statement, which explains why both cases count as constructive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מילה improves the child, just as fixing a utensil improves it, so it is a constructive act. The burning execution was done by melting a lead wick and pouring it in. Melting the wick is a useful act of cooking, just like cooking the dye herbs (סממנין) for the משכן. Since both acts accomplish something, they are מתקן and not מקלקל.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference is there to me? (meaning: they are the same)
To repair a vessel or utensil
A wick (here, the lead wick melted for the execution by burning)
Herbs cooked to make dyes for the משכן

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה, the proofs from מילה and the burning of a בת כהן do not work, because both acts are constructive. So his rule that every מקלקל is פטור stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון about מקלקל. It also teaches that whether an act is 'destructive' depends on whether it accomplishes something useful, not on how it looks.

phrases.english: For Rav Ashi said:
What difference is there to me between repairing through circumcision
and repairing a vessel?
What difference is there to me between cooking a wick
phrases.notes: The 'wick' here is the lead that was melted for the death penalty of burning.

phrases.english: and cooking herbs (for dyes)?
phrases.notes: Cooking dye herbs was one of the jobs done for the משכן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source and reasoning behind the answer in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that מילה and the burning execution are constructive acts.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אשי's comparisons: מילה is like repairing a vessel, and melting the wick is like cooking dye herbs in the משכן.

steps.title: How to show the measure of a double סיט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's measure for whitening, a double סיט, and gives two ways that אמוראים demonstrated it with their fingers.
steps.simpleTranslation: The measure for whitening, etc. רב יוסף demonstrated it doubled; רב חייא בר אמי demonstrated it single.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase about the measure for one who whitens. Then it reports how two אמוראים showed the size of a double סיט using their hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סיט is a gap between fingers. רב יוסף showed the gap between the index and middle fingers and said to double it. רב חייא בר אמי showed one larger gap, between the thumb and forefinger, which already equals a double סיט. Both agree on the size. They only show it in different ways.

keyTerms.meaning: Measure; the minimum amount needed to be חייב
One who whitens or bleaches (wool or cloth)
Demonstrates or shows
Doubled
Simple or single (one span)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a disagreement about the measure. Both אמוראים mean the same double סיט. They just show it differently.

phrases.english: The measure for one who whitens, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the earlier משנה, which gives the measure as the width of a double סיט.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef would demonstrate it doubled,
phrases.notes: The gap between index and middle finger, taken twice.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי מַחְוֵי פָּשׁוּט.
phrases.english: Rav Chiya bar Ami would demonstrate it simply (as one span).
phrases.notes: The gap between thumb and forefinger, which equals a double סיט.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the מקלקל discussion and returns to explain a measure from the earlier משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A double סיט is shown either by doubling the index–middle finger gap (רב יוסף) or by one thumb–forefinger span (רב חייא בר אמי).

steps.title: New משנה: trapping a bird or a deer
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. רבי יהודה says one who traps a bird into a closet, or a deer into a house, is חייב. The חכמים begin to answer and agree about the bird. Their full view continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי יהודה says: One who traps a bird into a closet, or a deer into a house, is חייב. And the חכמים say: a bird into a closet...
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens about the מלאכה of trapping (צידה) on שבת. רבי יהודה gives his view, and the חכמים start to give theirs. Their statement continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is what counts as trapping. For רבי יהודה, bringing a bird into a closet or a deer into a house counts, so the person is חייב. The חכמים agree about the bird in a closet. Their ruling on where a deer counts as trapped continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין, 'our משנה'; it marks the start of a new משנה
One who traps or hunts
A bird
A closet or cabinet (an enclosed storage space)
A deer
And the Sages say (introducing the majority opinion)

phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Yehuda says:
One who traps a bird into a closet,
and a deer into a house, is liable.
And the Rabbis say: a bird into a closet
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר הַצָּד צִפּוֹר לַמִּגְדָּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: the מלאכה of trapping.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: trapping a bird into a closet or a deer into a house makes one חייב. The חכמים agree about the bird into a closet, and their full view continues.
